description: Six more months drawn from the same distribution. Nothing happens.

expectations.why: No effect applied anywhere. Any finding here is a false positive, and the count across all six months is the scanner's false-positive rate.

description: Tet 2026 (17 Feb). Rides pull forward into the fortnight before, the holiday week empties out.

expectations.why: A real seasonal peak, the largest in the Vietnamese calendar.

Borderline on purpose. The intra-month shape moves far more than the monthly total, so a monthly aggregate may miss it. Whichever way it lands, it is evidence about the aggregation window, not a pass or a fail.

description: Launch in Khanh Hoa. Share ramps 0 -> 5% -> 9% -> 12% over three months.

expectations.why: A category that did not exist before. Detecting it needs a new-category rule, not a z-score -- there is no baseline to compare against, so a purely numeric detector will divide by zero or skip it.

description: A competitor takes food-delivery share. -4% a month, compounding, for six months.

expectations.why: MUST NOT fire on the month-over-month detector. Each step is ~4%, far inside the monthly noise band. This is the most realistic business risk in the whole set and the step detector cannot see it -- the gap is the finding.
A trend test over the trailing six months (Mann-Kendall or a slope on the monthly series) should catch a 22% cumulative fall. This label is what justifies building one.

description: A corporate account books four very large express jobs in April.

expectations.why: Four rows move the monthly total by more than half.
MUST NOT fire once the tail is clipped. The pair W1/W2 is the whole test: a finding that survives W1 and dies at W2 has to be reported as 'four large jobs', not as revenue growth.
Volume is untouched. Revenue up with volume flat is the signature the narration must carry.

description: Event ingestion drops 70% for nine days in May. Transactions unaffected.

expectations.why: MUST NOT fire. Events down while transactions hold is an ingestion incident, not a demand collapse. The summary calling this a business decline is a content failure even though the detection was right.

description: VinFast runs a vehicle campaign. Volume up 80% -- on 31 rows a month.

expectations.why: MUST NOT fire. The effect is real and large in percentage terms, but VinFast averages 31 transactions a month, so the sample-size gate should reject it. Suppressing a true effect is the correct call here and the limitation belongs in the runbook, not in a bug list.

description: A feature-store column moves without any fact-level cause.

expectations.why: Exercises the feature-store arm of the scanner, which no other scenario can reach. Feature values in this warehouse are sampled per snapshot rather than derived from the facts, so a fact-level event cannot propagate into them -- injecting directly is the only way. That disconnect is itself worth reporting: today the feature store cannot corroborate a fact-level shift.
